sources.entry: ftfy - Makes Unicode text less broken and more consistent automagically.

summary.one_liner: ftfy is a Python package that repairs mojibake (garbled text from encoding mix-ups) and makes Unicode text more consistent.
summary.what_it_does: The README shows ftfy fixing text with fix_text and fix_encoding, for example turning 'âœ” No problems' into '✔ No problems'. It can undo multiple stacked layers of mojibake in one pass. It can also handle mojibake that has curly quotes applied on top, and a non-breaking-space case where U+A0 became an ASCII space. It decodes HTML entities that appear outside HTML, including incorrectly capitalized ones like 'P&EACUTE;REZ'. The README says it avoids false positives: correctly decoded text such as 'IL Y MARQUÉ…' is left unchanged. Full documentation is hosted on readthedocs and covers configuration, fixer functions, and command-line usage.
use_cases: clean up scraped web text with encoding errors
fix mojibake in datasets before NLP processing
normalize Unicode text in a data pipeline
recover text mangled by Windows-1252 and UTF-8 mix-ups
decode stray HTML entities in plain text
notable: fix_text repairs multiple stacked layers of mojibake in one call
fix_encoding entry point for simple encoding repair
Conservative design that aims to avoid changing correctly decoded text
Also decodes HTML entities that appear outside HTML, even when miscapitalized
Citable record on Zenodo; widely cited in NLP research
caveats: The README states it is a Python 3 package
Documentation lives on an external readthedocs site, not in the README
License terms in the README add restrictions beyond standard Apache wording, including a prohibition on use in AI training datasets
summary.license: Apache (named in README; the README says the Apache license governs use)
